items.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020
items.q: I got so lucky to be around all these old musicians... I played a few tunes one time with Big Joe Turner.

ctx.x: Fine, thank you. Well before, to start things off, I just wrote down a short list of musicians you worked with during your career, and I’d like to enumerate some of them. There’s Milt Jackson, Harry Edison, Clark Terry, Johnny Griffin, Tommy Flanagan, Phil Woods, Bob Berg, Lou Donaldson, Hank Jones, and it goes on and on and on and on. What an impressive list. You must have so many memories, working with all those giants of jazz.

Yes of course, and I would say that I was young and old at the same time. What I mean is that when I started at that time, when I started to be really crazy, just crazy banana about jazz, the only thing we had was records. LPs and tapes. That was it. And especially being from the southwest of France there were no jazz schools. There was maybe at that time, when I moved to Paris in ’85 they started to have one jazz school over there. So it’s just to describe — so in other words whenever you, each of us, we wanted…
musicians. And the more, with the years — it’s been years — and now when I think of it, I mean I played a few tunes one time with Big Joe Turner.
